										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<p>Researchers at the National University of Singapore published a technical paper titled “CHIPSMORE: Compute-in-Interconnect and -Memory Chiplets for Multi-Mode Multi-Request LLM Inference Acceleration.”</p>
<p><strong>Abstract Excerpt:</strong></p>
<p>“This paper presents CHIPSMORE, a multi-mode and multi-request LLM inference accelerator that integrates compute-in-interconnect and CIM to support both base-mode and low-rank adaptation (LoRA) inference under diverse workloads. CHIPSMORE employs heterogeneous processing elements consisting of resistive RAM analog compute-in-memory (RRAM-ACIM) and static RAM digital compute-in-memory (SRAM-DCIM) interconnected through a programmable Inter-PE computational network (IPCN). ”</p>
<p><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.30509">Find the technical paper here</a>. August 2026.</p>
<p>Chong, Yue Jiet, Yimin Wang, Zhen Wu, Zixuan Wang, Wei Zhang, and Xuanyao Fong. “CHIPSMORE: Compute-in-Interconnect and -Memory Chiplets for Multi-Mode Multi-Request LLM Inference Acceleration.” arXiv preprint arXiv:2608.30509 (August 2026). https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2608.30509</p>

					<description><![CDATA[<p>Researchers at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute and IBM T.J. Watson Research Center published a technical paper titled “REACH: Controller-Managed Long-Span ECC for HBM AI Inference.” Abstract Excerpt: “High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) cost motivates stronger controller protection that can support a wider range of device error rates.High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) cost motivates stronger controller protection that can support a... <a class="read_more" href="https://semiengineering.com/reducing-hbm-ecc-controller-overhead-for-ai-inference-rpi-ibm/">&#187; read more</a></p>
<p>The post <a href="https://semiengineering.com/reducing-hbm-ecc-controller-overhead-for-ai-inference-rpi-ibm/">Reducing HBM ECC Controller Overhead For AI Inference (RPI, IBM)</a> appeared first on <a href="https://semiengineering.com">Semiconductor Engineering</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<p>Researchers at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute and IBM T.J. Watson Research Center published a technical paper titled “REACH: Controller-Managed Long-Span ECC for HBM AI Inference.”</p>
<p><strong>Abstract Excerpt:</strong> “High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) cost motivates stronger controller protection that can support a wider range of device error rates.High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) cost motivates stronger controller protection that can support a wider range of device error rates. Long-span error-correcting codes provide stronger protection at a comparable code rate, but a direct implementation couples small accesses to span-wide state and requires costly decoding at HBM bandwidth. Read-dominated LLM decode offers a favorable setting: sequential reads support span aggregation, while sparse writes limit parity-update traffic. This paper presents REACH, a controller microarchitecture that uses established inner codes to correct common errors and identify unresolved chunks, reserving a long outer code for known-erasure repair.”</p>
<p><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10861">Find the technical paper here</a>. September 2026.</p>
<p>Xie, Rui, Yunhua Fang, Asad Ul Haq, Linsen Ma, Sanchari Sen, Swagath Venkataramani, Liu Liu, and Tong Zhang. “REACH: Controller-Managed Long-Span ECC for HBM AI Inference.” arXiv preprint arXiv:2609.10861 (September 2026). https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2609.10861</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>The post <a href="https://semiengineering.com/reducing-hbm-ecc-controller-overhead-for-ai-inference-rpi-ibm/">Reducing HBM ECC Controller Overhead For AI Inference (RPI, IBM)</a> appeared first on <a href="https://semiengineering.com">Semiconductor Engineering</a>.</p>

					<description><![CDATA[<p>Researchers at National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University and TSMC published a technical paper titled “High contrast EUV imaging enabled by topological quasi phase-only masks.” Abstract Excerpt: “Here, we propose a paradigm shift in EUV PSM technology by introducing molybdenum (Mo)-based quasi phase-only masks (quasi-POMs) with high reflectivity and minimal absorption. Through rigorous electromagnetic simulations,... <a class="read_more" href="https://semiengineering.com/molybdenum-quasi-phase-only-masks-improve-euv-imaging-nycu-tsmc/">&#187; read more</a></p>
<p>The post <a href="https://semiengineering.com/molybdenum-quasi-phase-only-masks-improve-euv-imaging-nycu-tsmc/">Molybdenum Quasi Phase-Only Masks Improve EUV Imaging (NYCU, TSMC)</a> appeared first on <a href="https://semiengineering.com">Semiconductor Engineering</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Researchers at National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University and TSMC published a technical paper titled “High contrast EUV imaging enabled by topological quasi phase-only masks.”</p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Abstract Excerpt:</strong> “Here, we propose a paradigm shift in EUV PSM technology by introducing molybdenum (Mo)-based quasi phase-only masks (quasi-POMs) with high reflectivity and minimal absorption. Through rigorous electromagnetic simulations, we demonstrate that Mo quasi-POMs deliver up to 35% higher image contrast, a fivefold increase in common focus window, and 92% lower peak telecentricity error than conventional tantalum (Ta)-based absorbers, enabling 12.5-nm half-pitch resolution for 0.33 numerical aperture (NA) EUV systems with monopole illumination.”</p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><a href="https://doi.org/10.1364/OE.607043">Find the technical paper here</a>. August 2026.</p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Po-Hsun Fang, Pokai Chang, Chaowei Huang, Lee-Feng Chen, Yen-Liang Chen, and Peichen Yu, &#8220;High contrast EUV imaging enabled by topological quasi phase-only masks,&#8221; Opt. Express 34, 30091-30105 (2026)</p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">&nbsp;</p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">&nbsp;</p>

										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Researchers at imec, KU Leuven, and ASM published a technical paper titled “Dissecting the transition metal dichalcogenides-based metal-oxide-semiconductor structures charge components.”</p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Abstract Excerpt:</strong> “Different variable charges such as interface traps, oxide border traps, and mobile carriers can contribute to the total capacitance in metal oxide semiconductor (MOS) field-effect devices. This study aims to quantify these charge components using multi-frequency, multi-temperature capacitance–voltage/conductance–voltage (C–V/G–V) scans with interface trap density profile mapping combined with Hall measurements on fully depleted few-layer transition metal dichalcogenides (MX<sub>2</sub>)-based MOS devices.”</p>

					<description><![CDATA[<p>Researchers at the NIST, UCSD et al. published a technical paper titled “Predicting Cure Evolution and Thermal Endurance of a Highly Filled Epoxy Underfill for Advanced Packaging.” Abstract Excerpt: “Epoxy underfill materials are critical to advanced semiconductor packaging by enhancing mechanical integrity, redistributing thermomechanical stresses, and improving solder-joint reliability in flip-chip and other fine-pitch interconnect... <a class="read_more" href="https://semiengineering.com/modeling-predicts-cure-and-thermal-endurance-of-advanced-packaging-underfill-nist-ucsd-et-al/">&#187; read more</a></p>
<p>The post <a href="https://semiengineering.com/modeling-predicts-cure-and-thermal-endurance-of-advanced-packaging-underfill-nist-ucsd-et-al/">Modeling Predicts Cure And Thermal Endurance Of Advanced Packaging Underfill (NIST, UCSD et al.)</a> appeared first on <a href="https://semiengineering.com">Semiconductor Engineering</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<p>Researchers at the NIST, UCSD et al. published a technical paper titled “Predicting Cure Evolution and Thermal Endurance of a Highly Filled Epoxy Underfill for Advanced Packaging.”</p>
<p><strong>Abstract Excerpt:</strong> “Epoxy underfill materials are critical to advanced semiconductor packaging by enhancing mechanical integrity, redistributing thermomechanical stresses, and improving solder-joint reliability in flip-chip and other fine-pitch interconnect architectures. Their performance is strongly influenced by cure evolution during processing and thermal stability during service, making quantitative evaluation important for process optimization and long-term reliability assessment. The cure kinetics and thermal degradation behavior of a highly-filled epoxy underfill were investigated using differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), and diffusion-incorporated kinetic modeling. Isoconversional analysis showed that the apparent activation energy varied with conversion and increased sharply at high conversion, indicating multi-step cure behavior and diffusion control. A two-step modified Kamal–Sourour model incorporating diffusion control in the second step improved prediction of conversion after vitrification and was used to predict cure evolution under a designed oven cure schedule, which achieved nearly complete cure. Cryomilling improved TGA reproducibility without causing detectable chemical changes. Analysis following the ASTM E1641/E1877 protocols revealed a strong temperature dependence of estimated thermal endurance based on a 5% mass-loss criterion under nitrogen. Together, the results provide a quantitative framework for predicting cure evolution under practical thermal schedules, evaluating late-stage diffusion effects, and estimating degradation-based thermal endurance for highly-filled industrial thermosets.”</p>
<p>Find the <a href="https://www.nist.gov/publications/predicting-cure-evolution-and-thermal-endurance-highly-filled-epoxy-underfill-advanced">technical paper here</a>. August 2026.</p>
<p>Tao, R. , Giang, R. , Moukhina, E. , Forster, A. , Cho, T. , Centellas, P. , Romberg, S. , Tsinas, Z. and Soles, C. (2026), Predicting Cure Evolution and Thermal Endurance of a Highly Filled Epoxy Underfill for Advanced Packaging, Journal Of Polymer Science, [online], https://doi.org/10.1002/pola.70283, https://tsapps.nist.gov/publication/get_pdf.cfm?pub_id=962138</p>

		<title>HW Information-Flow Tracking for Pre-Silicon Security Testing (Princeton, MIT, EPFL)</title>

		<pubDate>Fri, 11 Sep 2026 20:15:35 +0000</pubDate>

					<description><![CDATA[<p>Researchers at Princeton University, MIT CSAIL, and EPFL published a technical paper titled “Efficient Hardware Information-Flow Tracking for Pre-Silicon Security Testing.” Abstract “Register-Transfer Level (RTL) simulation is widely used to test hardware before it is fabricated. To allow testing for security related information flow properties, such as confidentiality and integrity, taint logic can be automatically... <a class="read_more" href="https://semiengineering.com/hw-information-flow-tracking-for-pre-silicon-security-testing-princeton-mit-epfl/">&#187; read more</a></p>
<p>The post <a href="https://semiengineering.com/hw-information-flow-tracking-for-pre-silicon-security-testing-princeton-mit-epfl/">HW Information-Flow Tracking for Pre-Silicon Security Testing (Princeton, MIT, EPFL)</a> appeared first on <a href="https://semiengineering.com">Semiconductor Engineering</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<p>Researchers at Princeton University, MIT CSAIL, and EPFL published a technical paper titled “Efficient Hardware Information-Flow Tracking for Pre-Silicon Security Testing.”</p>
<p><strong>Abstract </strong></p>
<p>“Register-Transfer Level (RTL) simulation is widely used to test hardware before it is fabricated. To allow testing for security related information flow properties, such as confidentiality and integrity, taint logic can be automatically added to the design to track how information flows through it. However, taint logic instrumented by the state-of-the-art, such as CellIFT, makes simulation-based testing prohibitively expensive: On our evaluation of Mega-BOOM (136K cells), it increases the instrumented design to 5.81x the original cell count and causes a 143.72x simulation slowdown. The taint logic could be simplified to improve simulation speed, but it will inevitably trade off its precision. This lightweight, imprecise taint logic will introduce false positives and may eventually result in even more overhead to check these false positives. This paper explores the research question of where precision is actually needed in the design to overcome the overhead of false positives. It presents CEGAR-T, a framework that automatically synthesizes taint logic that minimizes the taint-logic instrumentation overhead while guaranteeing no false positives (relative to the precise CellIFT baseline). We have implemented CEGAR-T and evaluated it on the safe instruction set problem for timing side-channel security across open-source RISC-V cores. Over all evaluated cores, CEGAR-T reduces both instrumentation and simulation overhead, in geometric-mean, from 5.64x to 1.42x and from 34.65x to 1.79x, respectively, without compromising the precision benefit of the CellIFT baseline.”</p>
<p><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.06791">Find the technical paper here</a>. September 2026.</p>
<p>Fan, Yu-Wei, Yuheng Yang, Christine Guo, SooHyuk Cho, Thomas Bourgeat, Mengjia Yan, and Sharad Malik. “Efficient Hardware Information-Flow Tracking for Pre-Silicon Security Testing.” arXiv preprint arXiv:2609.06791 (September 2026). https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2609.06791</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>The post <a href="https://semiengineering.com/hw-information-flow-tracking-for-pre-silicon-security-testing-princeton-mit-epfl/">HW Information-Flow Tracking for Pre-Silicon Security Testing (Princeton, MIT, EPFL)</a> appeared first on <a href="https://semiengineering.com">Semiconductor Engineering</a>.</p>

<p>The post <a href="https://semiengineering.com/chip-industry-week-in-review-155/">Chip Industry Week in Review</a> appeared first on <a href="https://semiengineering.com">Semiconductor Engineering</a>.</p>

										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<h3><strong>SPIE </strong></h3>
<p>News from this week’s <strong>SPIE Photomask Technology + Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography</strong> <a href="https://spie.org/conferences-and-exhibitions/photomask-technology-and-extreme-ultraviolet-lithography">conference</a>:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>ASML</strong> and <strong>TSMC</strong> are launching an industry initiative to <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AVcTQ0S7EMQ">transition high-NA EUV lithography</a> from current 6-inch photomasks to larger <a href="https://pr.cld.tsmc.com/english/news/3338">12-inch masks</a>, which could improve scanner productivity and eliminate some stitching constraints. The companies are targeting a 12-inch mask pilot line by 2031, with production-ready systems by 2033. TSMC plans to begin using high-NA EUV in high-volume manufacturing in 2030.</li>
<li>The <strong>eBeam Initiative</strong>&#8216;s annual <a href="https://www.ebeam.org/docs/ebeam-initiative-bacus-2026-roundup-release-final.pdf">industry survey</a> found 66% of semiconductor experts expect large-format photomasks to be adopted within a decade, while 94% expect mask revenue to grow this year.</li>
<li><strong>imec</strong> demonstrated <a href="https://www.imec-int.com/en/press/imec-demonstrates-extension-chemically-amplified-resists-high-na-euv-lithography">single-exposure high-NA EUV patterning</a> of 22nm-pitch lines/spaces and 28nm-pitch vias using established chemically amplified resist technology, supporting layers envisioned for A14/A10 logic.</li>
<li><strong>Intel Foundry</strong> and <strong>ASML</strong> said high-NA EUV has now processed more than <a href="https://www.asml.com/en/news/press-releases/2026/intel-foundry-and-asml-collaborate-to-accelerate-industry-readiness-for-high-na-euv">1 million wafers</a>, including select production layers for Panther Lake, with Intel 18A high-NA layers meeting or exceeding comparable patterns made with conventional EUV.</li>
<li><strong>Samsung</strong> formally joined the <a href="https://news.samsungsemiconductor.com/global/samsung-electronics-and-asml-expand-strategic-collaboration-for-next-generation-semiconductor-manufacturing/">12-inch photomask initiative</a> and says it plans to introduce high-NA EUV into DRAM high-volume manufacturing in 2028.</li>
<li><strong>D2S</strong> highlighted new PLDC techniques for <a href="https://design2silicon.com/products/pldc/">improving mask uniformity and linearity</a>, including Dynamic Maximum Dose, variable bias correction, and offline processing.</li>
<li><strong>NY Creates</strong> joined the industry initiative developing <a href="https://ny-creates.org/ny-creates-announces-participation-in-12-inch-mask-industry-initiative/">12-inch photomasks</a> for high-NA EUV.</li>
</ul>
<h3><strong>Arm broadens its AI push</strong></h3>
<p>At its <strong>Arm </strong>Everywhere conference in China, the company announced:</p>
<ul>
<li>A next-gen <a href="https://newsroom.arm.com/news/arm-css-for-mobile-2-agentic-ai-mobile-graphics">edge AI platform</a>, Arm Compute Subsystems for Mobile 2, aimed at agentic AI and cinematic mobile graphics. It features Mali G2-Ultra NX neural accelerator GPU and CPU cluster technology with scalable matrix extension 2.</li>
<li>A <a href="https://newsroom.arm.com/news/arm-total-design-and-robotics-capability-framework-for-physical-ai">physical AI ecosystem program</a>, Arm Total Design for Physical AI, for multiple companies across the technology stack, to boost development of robotics.</li>
<li>Neoverse CSS N4 for <a href="https://newsroom.arm.com/news/arm-agi-cpu-neoverse-css-n4-agentic-ai">AI infrastructure</a> with up to 128 cores per die, supporting LPDDR6, PCIe 7, and delivering up to 2X the performance, complemented by the Arm AGI CPU.</li>
<li>An <a href="https://newsroom.arm.com/news/arm-unveils-arm-ai-portal">AI portal to connect developers</a> and optimize apps across its compute platform.</li>
</ul>
<h3><strong>New capacity</strong></h3>
<ul>
<li><strong>Amkor</strong> announced <a href="https://ir.amkor.com/news-releases/news-release-details/amkor-technology-announces-phase-2-arizona-advanced-packaging">phase 2</a> of its Arizona advanced packaging and test campus, adding 60,000 square meters of cleanroom space and increasing the planned investment to approximately $12B. Construction is expected to begin in late 2027.</li>
<li><strong>ASML</strong> has begun work on a <a href="https://www.asml.com/en/news/press-releases/2026/asml-begins-construction-of-new-eindhoven-campus">new campus</a> at Brainport Industries Campus North near Eindhoven, creating a second major site to support future manufacturing growth beyond its Veldhoven headquarters.</li>
</ul>
<h3><strong>Memory</strong></h3>
<ul>
<li data-start="187" data-end="650"><strong>SK hynix</strong> outlined a strategy spanning HBM, 3D DRAM, HBF, CXL and SSDs, with memory increasingly co-designed at the system level for AI. The company identified <a href="https://news.skhynix.com/en/future-forum-2026/">3D memory as a key</a> future technology.</li>
<li><strong>Kepler Computing</strong> emerged from stealth with its new high-bandwidth <a href="https://www.linkedin.com/posts/we-are-proud-to-announce-kepler-our-mission-share-7503533331792183296-zepk/">AI memory architecture</a> using 3D stacking and ferroelectric materials. The company, which raised $468M, claims an order of magnitude capacity increase compared to SRAM and HBM, and expects to ramp production next year.</li>
<li><a href="https://www.trendforce.com/presscenter/news/20260907-13219.html">Global DRAM industry revenue</a> jumped ~60% sequentially to nearly $155B in Q2. Market share leaders: <strong>Samsung</strong> 39%, <strong>SK hynix</strong> 25% and <strong>Micron</strong> 23%.</li>
<li class="PDq2pG_selectionAnchorContainer" data-start="187" data-end="650">Chinese AI-chip suppliers including <strong>Huawei </strong>and <strong>Cambricon </strong>are <a href="https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/chinas-ai-chipmakers-raise-prices-high-bandwidth-memory-shortage-bites-2026-09-10/">raising accelerator prices</a> as limited access to HBM drives up costs.</li>
<li data-start="187" data-end="650"><strong>Memory research</strong>: <strong>USC</strong>-led researchers developed a vertically stackable vdW memory selector with &gt;10¹²-cycle endurance, sub-20 ns switching and low device variability, addressing a key challenge in scaling <a href="https://www.nature.com/articles/s41928-026-01704-2">high-density 3D memory</a>. <strong>NUS</strong> researchers developed an on-chip pulse generator for field-free magnetic switching, cutting write energy by four orders of magnitude and pointing to faster, <a href="https://www.nature.com/articles/s41928-026-01699-w">lower-power magnetic memory</a>.</li>
</ul>
<h3><strong>Big deals</strong></h3>
<ul>
<li><strong>Qualcomm</strong> and <strong>Amazon</strong> <a href="https://www.qualcomm.com/news/releases/2026/09/qualcomm-announces-multi-generational-product-collaboration-with">inked a deal</a> worth up to $60B to create <a href="https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/804328/000110465926105718/tm2623289d1_8k.htm">custom silicon for large-scale AI data centers and AI inference</a>, along with optical connectivity up to 1.6T, and future solutions.</li>
<li><strong>Analog Devices</strong> <a href="https://www.analog.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2026/9-9-2026-adi-to-acquire-alif-semiconductor.html">agreed to acquire</a> <strong>Alif Semiconductor</strong> in an all-cash transaction for $1.35B, for its high-efficiency AI-native MCUs and fusion processors optimized for on-device, physical AI.</li>
<li><strong>OpenAI</strong> is working with <strong>Samsung </strong>on <a href="https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/openai-says-working-with-samsung-next-generation-chips-deepening-cooperation-2026-09-09/">next-gen chips</a>, with OpenAI Korea chief Harrison Kim saying the companies have made significant progress in joint production and research, reports Reuters.</li>
</ul>
<h3><strong>Raking it in</strong></h3>
<ul>
<li><strong>Ayar Labs</strong> raised $150M and announced <strong>Wiwynn</strong> made a strategic investment earlier this year for its continued transition to high-volume manufacturing of <a href="https://ayarlabs.com/news/ayar-labs-expands-2026-funding-to-650-million/">CPO for AI scale-up</a>.</li>
<li><strong>Positron AI</strong> raised $875M for its <a href="https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/positron-ai-raises-875-million-at-a-5-billion-valuation-to-bring-its-next-generation-inference-silicon-to-market-302874601.html">memory-first inference silicon</a> built on commodity LPDDR5X.</li>
<li><strong>Fab2</strong> raised $500M to <a href="https://www.linkedin.com/posts/fab2-raised-a-500m-series-a-at-37b-valuation-share-7503130916056117249-7mb9/?utm_source=share&amp;utm_medium=member_desktop&amp;rcm=ACoAABOPdcUBencoQUXWuZEfl7vLLaQ8XnFxUCQ">mass-produce semiconductor fabs</a>.</li>
<li><strong>Celero Communications</strong> raised $275M for its 1.6T to next-gen 3.2T <a href="https://celero.inc/celero-communications-raises-275-million-series-c-following-validation-of-industrys-first-2nm-coherent-dsp-silicon/">AI optical interconnects</a>, after validating 2nm coherent DSP silicon.</li>
</ul>
<h3><strong>Quantum developments</strong></h3>
<ul>
<li><strong>imec</strong> demonstrated <a href="https://www.imec-int.com/en/press/imec-advances-scalable-superconducting-technology-world-first-nbtin-circuits-and-30nm">three-metal-level NbTiN Josephson-junction circuits</a> with densities of 3.8 million junctions/cm² and superconducting interconnects scaled to 30nm.</li>
<li><strong>Xanadu</strong> and <strong>ASML</strong> will collaborate on <a href="https://investors.xanadu.ai/news-releases/news-release-details/xanadu-and-asml-announce-collaboration-advance-lithography">advanced lithography</a> for photonic quantum chips to improve patterning and reduce optical loss.</li>
<li>The <strong>U.S. Department of Commerce</strong> finalized $775M in previously announced CHIPS R&amp;D awards for domestic quantum semiconductor development and manufacturing, including <a href="https://investors.gf.com/news-releases/news-release-details/globalfoundries-and-us-department-commerce-finalize-375m-rd">$375M for GlobalFoundries</a> and $100M each for <a href="https://investors.rigetti.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rigetti-signs-definitive-agreement-100m-us-government-accelerate">Rigetti</a>, <a href="https://www.dwavequantum.com/company/newsroom/press-release/d-wave-finalizes-agreement-with-u-s-department-of-commerce-for-up-to-100-million/">D-Wave</a>, <a href="https://www.psiquantum.com/news-import/psiquantum-finalizes-100-million-award-with-the-us-department-of-commerce">PsiQuantum</a>, and <a href="https://ir.quantinuum.com/news-releases/news-release-details/quantinuum-finalizes-100-million-chips-rd-award-us-department">Quantinuum</a>.</li>
</ul>
<h3><strong>Market data</strong></h3>
<ul>
<li>Revenue for the <a href="https://www.trendforce.com/presscenter/news/20260909-13225.html">world’s top 10 foundries</a> rose more than 11% sequentially to a record ~$53B in Q2, according to <strong>TrendForce</strong>.</li>
<li>
<div class="" data-turn-id-container="02db4e99-11c6-4028-a9be-f19d1eff42cd" data-is-intersecting="true"><a href="https://www.semiconductors.org/global-semiconductor-sales-increase-6-4-month-to-month-in-july/">Global semiconductor sales</a> reached $147B in July, up 135% YoY, according to the <strong>SIA</strong>.</div>
</li>
<li>The <a href="https://www.yolegroup.com/press-release/data-centers-set-to-drive-a-1-5-trillion-semiconductor-market-by-2031/">data-center semiconductor market</a> will reach $1.5T by 2031 as AI drives increasing demand for logic, memory, optical interconnects and power devices, predicts <strong>Yole Group</strong>. Advanced packaging and HBM capacity are emerging as major bottlenecks, while AI rack power could approach <a href="https://semiengineering.com/the-1-megawatt-rack-debate/">1 MW</a> by the end of the decade.</li>
</ul>

<ul>
<li><a href="https://pr.tsmc.com/english/news/3340">TSMC</a> (August revenue up 53% YoY) and <a href="https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2026/2026-interim-results/">IQE </a>(1st half up 40% YoY).</li>

<h2 id="Global"><strong>Global</strong></h2>
<h3><strong>Europe</strong></h3>
<ul>
<li><strong>The U.K. government</strong> released an expanded <a href="https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/semiconductor-sector-study">study of the country’s semiconductor sector</a>, identifying 703 companies and estimating that dedicated semiconductor businesses generated £10.6B in revenue in 2025.</li>
<li><strong>SEMI Europe</strong> published a <a href="https://www.semi.org/sites/semi.org/files/2026-09/SEMI_Europe_Position_Paper_ChipsAct2.0.pdf">position paper</a> outlining nine recommendations for the EU Chips Act 2.0, including broader First-of-a-Kind eligibility, six-month permitting timelines, and measures addressing energy, infrastructure, and manufacturing costs. It also called for balanced funding, so leading-edge projects don’t crowd out pilot lines, mature and specialty technologies, and advanced packaging.</li>
<li>
<div>
<div>
<div>

<h2 id="New Technologies"><strong>New Technologies</strong></h2>
<p><b>PDF Solutions</b> debuted <span draggable="true"><a href="https://www.pdf.com/resources/introducing-exensio-aurora-pdf-solutions-unveils-highly-scalable-architecture-for-exensio-analytics/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Exensio Aurora</a></span>, its new scalable analytics architecture. The product is designed to handle semiconductor manufacturing data at petabyte scale and securely deploy agentic AI across manufacturing operations and the supply chain.</p>
<p><strong>Taiyo Holdings</strong> and <strong>imec</strong> demonstrated a 3-layer RDL with 700nm wiring and vias on 300mm wafers using Taiyo’s new photosensitive dielectric material. The work advances <a href="https://prtimes.jp/main/html/rd/p/000000174.000028282.html">fine-pitch RDL technology</a> for advanced packaging.</p>
<p><b>Infineon</b> introduced the <span draggable="true"><a href="https://www.infineon.com/technology-news/2026/inftn202609-136" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">TDA235E5 and TDA235E0</a></span>, a dual-phase smart power stage family designed to meet growing power density requirements of next-generation AI accelerators and vertical power delivery modules. The new offerings will deliver benchmark power density exceeding 2 A/mm².</p>
<p><strong>imec</strong> has moved its <a href="https://www.imec-int.com/en/articles/integration-ready-96-band-linescan-sensor-sets-new-standard-chip-hyperspectral-imaging">96-band hyperspectral linescan sensor</a> into commercial availability for camera and satellite developers. The CMOS-based sensor has a spectral range of 450 to 900nm, improves signal-to-noise ratio by 40% over its predecessor, and integrates its spectral filters directly on-chip.</p>
<p><strong>CoreWeave </strong>launched “<a href="https://www.coreweave.com/news/coreweave-launches-physical-ai-field-engineering-to-turn-proprietary-data-into-production-ai">Physical AI Field Engineering</a>” this week, a new offering built to help manufacturers integrate physical AI into their engineering processes.</p>
<h3><strong>Smartphone chips</strong></h3>
<ul>
<li><strong>Apple</strong> unveiled new products under new CEO, John Ternus, including its <a href="https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/09/apple-debuts-iphone-18-pro-and-iphone-18-pro-max/">2nm A20 Pro chip</a> for the iPhone 18 with 50% more memory bandwidth and integrated neural accelerators, as well as the company&#8217;s first <a href="https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/09/apple-unveils-iphone-duo/">foldable phone</a>, iPhone Duo.</li>
<li>Powering its new Mate XT 2 trifold smartphone,<strong> Huawei </strong>launched the first commercial application of its Kirin 9050 <a href="https://www.scmp.com/tech/big-tech/article/3366669/huaweis-new-kirin-chip-puts-logic-folding-test-bigger-ambitions-ai">Pro chip with LogicFolding architecture</a>, with 42% better performance than its predecessor, per SCMP. (Read a related technical paper: Huawei’s <a href="https://arxiv.org/html/2609.04287v1">Tao Chip</a> Was Supposed to Melt?)</li>
</ul>
<h3><strong>Connecting data centers</strong></h3>
<ul>
<li><strong>OIF</strong> published the implementation agreement for <a href="https://www.oiforum.com/oif-releases-critical-1600zr-coherent-interface-ia-doubling-capacity-per-wavelength-for-data-center-interconnects/">1600ZR Coherent Interfaces</a>, doubling the capacity of its 800ZR specification.</li>
<li><strong>Meta </strong>and <strong>Panmnesia</strong> proposed an architecture that lets an <a href="https://panmnesia.com/news/en/2026-09-08-panmnesia-meta-nree-eng/">entire data center operate as one chip</a> by placing CPUs, accelerators, and memory in a single CXL-over-optics-based domain, with a high-fan-out non-blocking switch, a link acceleration unit and a fabric controller to bound latency variability.</li>
</ul>
<h3><strong>Adoptions and certifications</strong></h3>
<ul>
<li><strong>Cadence</strong> <a href="https://community.cadence.com/cadence_blogs_8/b/corporate-news/posts/accelerate-chip-design-with-arm-architecture-cadence-eda-tools-on-aws-graviton">qualified</a> its EDA tool flow to run natively on <strong>AWS</strong> Graviton, including front-end design and verification, synthesis, place-and-route, and timing sign-off. <strong>Annapurna Labs</strong> is now designing future-gen Graviton CPUs using the Cadence flow.</li>
<li>Japan&#8217;s <strong>NanoBridge Semiconductor</strong> adopted <strong>Siemens EDA</strong>’s <a href="https://news.siemens.com/en-us/siemens-precision-fpga-nanobridge/">FPGA tools</a> for its low-power, harsh-environment FPGAs for aerospace, automotive, and critical infrastructure.</li>
<li><strong>d-Matrix</strong> will use <strong>NVIDIA’s</strong> <a href="https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/chip-startup-d-matrix-use-nvidia-chip-linking-tech-ai-servers-2026-09-10/">NVLink Fusion</a> to connect its upcoming Raptor inference processors directly into NVIDIA-based data center systems. Raptor is expected to complete final design this year, with compatible rack-scale systems targeted for 2027.</li>
<li><strong>Redington </strong>will distribute <strong>Siemens EDA&#8217;s</strong> Xcelerator portfolio of <a href="https://news.siemens.com/en-us/siemens-redington-africa/">industrial software</a> across <strong>Africa</strong>.</li>

<h2 id="Research"><strong>Research</strong></h2>
<p><strong>Kyocera</strong> and <strong>Tohoku University</strong> developed an <a href="https://global.kyocera.com/newsroom/news/2026/001197.html">isolator-integrated photonics chip</a> that reduces back-reflected light by about 95%, enabling faster, energy-efficient AI data centers.</p>
<p><strong>CEA-Leti</strong>, <strong>Spintec</strong>, and <strong>Université Paris-Saclay</strong> researchers demonstrated a <a href="https://www.leti-cea.com/cea-tech/leti/english/Pages/What's-On/Press%20release/PR-Nature-Communications-Paper.aspx">hybrid nanoelectronic</a> Ising machine — combining hafnium-oxide ReRAM devices with stochastic MTJs — with an intrinsic annealing mechanism that could pave the way for more compact, faster, and energy-efficient hardware accelerators.</p>
<p><strong>Harvard</strong> researchers <a href="https://seas.harvard.edu/news/new-device-design-could-miniaturize-photonics-quantum-technologies">co-designed a layered semiconductor and a metasurface</a>, so every part of the device, including electronic states, optical fields, and geometry, works together toward efficient frequency conversion at a given wavelength, which could help miniaturize photonics and quantum technologies.</p>
<p>Researchers in Japan have demonstrated the first epitaxial growth of single-crystalline polar wurtzite <a href="https://www.tus.ac.jp/en/mediarelations/archive/20260904_0104.html">NbAlN</a> on GaN. An optimized NbAlN/GaN heterostructure more than tripled sheet electron density while retaining high room-temperature mobility, suggesting a potential new route to higher-performance GaN power and RF devices.</p>

<h2 id="Security"><strong>Security</strong></h2>
<h3><strong>AI threats</strong></h3>
<ul>
<li><strong>Google</strong> published new warnings on <a href="https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/from-prompting-to-autonomy-the-evolution-of-adversarial-ai">agentic AI-enabled cyberthreats</a> this week, sounding alarms for expanded SW supply chain risks, threats to AI IP, and increased LLMjacking efforts.</li>
<li>Independent researchers found that a swarm of <strong>OpenAI</strong> agents reportedly <a href="https://collusion.wiki/">hacked a German wiki site to create a message board</a> earlier this year, in an incident that appears to have preceded the similar <strong>Hugging Face</strong> breach in July.</li>
<li><strong>Anthropic</strong> published an updated cybersecurity advisory after discovering <a href="https://www.anthropic.com/research/alignment-assessment-cybersecurity-incidents">a fourth instance</a> of a Claude model gaining unauthorized access to a third-party system.</li>
<li><strong>AWS </strong>released <a href="https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/the-state-of-ai-for-security-measuring-what-matters-most-for-building-trust/">Deception Benchmark</a>, a new framework designed to test whether AI models can “distinguish real vulnerabilities from code that looks risky but is actually safe.”</li>
<li><a href="https://www.iaps.ai/research/accelerating-ai-data-center-security">A new IAPS report</a> on AI data center security called for new industry security standards, increased cross-company incident intelligence sharing, and security-focused supply chain realignment in the face of emerging AI threats to data centers.</li>
</ul>
<h3><strong>Alerts and advisories</strong></h3>
<ul>
<li><strong>Microsoft</strong> patched <a href="https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/releaseNote/2026-Sep">a record number of security vulnerabilities</a> this week, fixing 974 total flaws.</li>
<li>The <strong>FBI</strong> published its first-ever <a href="https://www.fbi.gov/investigate/cyber/cyber-strategy">cyber strategy roadmap</a>, with the document outlining a shift toward more proactive cybercrime disruption efforts.</li>
<li><strong>Cisco</strong> updated its Secure Firewall Management Center advisory to confirm active exploitation of a critical <a href="https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-onprem-fmc-authbypass-5JPp45V2">authentication-bypass vulnerability</a> that can let unauthenticated remote attackers gain root access.</li>
<li><strong>CERT Polska</strong> warned that attackers are actively exploiting a chain of six <a href="https://cert.pl/en/posts/2026/09/vulnerabilities-in-mikrotik-routeros-actively-exploited/">MikroTik RouterOS</a> vulnerabilities. Two flaws can be combined to take full control of exposed routers through SSH without authentication.</li>
<li>The <strong>NSA</strong>, <strong>FBI</strong>, and<strong> CISA</strong> issued a joint advisory covering cybersecurity threats tied to Chinese AI companies conducting industrial-scale distillation campaigns against US frontier AI models. Chinese companies have “<a href="https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/news/cisa-nsa-and-fbi-warn-china-based-ai-companies-targeting-us-ai-models-industrial-scale-knowledge">likely extracted billions of tokens </a>across millions of exchanges/requests from U.S. frontier AI models” since 2024, the agencies said.</li>
<li>CISA also updated its <a href="https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/news/cisa-releases-updated-insider-threat-guide-new-insights-mitigate-physical-and-cyber-threats">Insider Threat Mitigation Guide</a> for physical and cyber threats. All of CISA’s alerts for the week are <a href="https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories">here</a>.</li>
</ul>

<h2 id="Quantum"><strong>Quantum</strong></h2>
<p><strong>SkyWater </strong>launched <a href="https://www.skywatertechnology.com/skywater-launches-quantum-solutions-offering-to-advance-quantum-technologies-from-breakthrough-to-industrial-scale/">SkyWater Quantum Solutions</a>, combining superconducting, quantum photonics, heterogeneous integration, and advanced packaging capabilities to help move quantum technologies into manufacturing.</p>
<p><strong>Fujitsu </strong>developed a working prototype of a <a href="https://global.fujitsu/en-global/pr/news/2026/09/08-01">diamond-spin quantum computer</a> that incorporates tin-vacancy (SnV) centers into photonic ICs, an important step toward a modular architecture.</p>
<p><strong>IonQ</strong> released Superion 256, an upgradeable platform designed to scale <a href="https://www.ionq.com/news/ionq-launches-superion-product-line-industry-leading-upgradeable-platform-designed-to-scale-manufacturable-fault-tolerant-quantum-computing">manufacturable fault tolerant quantum</a> computing. It also published a fully compiled blueprint for breaking <a href="https://www.ionq.com/news/ionq-publishes-worlds-first-fully-compiled-end-to-end-blueprint-for-breaking-256-bit-elliptic-curve-signatures">256-bit elliptic-curve signatures,</a> and partnered with Congruity360 to boost <a href="https://www.ionq.com/news/ionq-and-congruity360-partner-to-enhance-quantum-safe-protection">quantum-safe protection</a>.</p>
<p><strong>LUMI AI Factory</strong> selected <strong>IQM</strong>’s staged path to deploy the EU&#8217;s first <a href="https://iqm.tech/press-releases/lumi-ai-factory-selects-iqms-staged-path-to-europes-first-superconducting-quantum-computer-with-logical-qubits/">superconducting quantum computer</a> with logical qubits, at <strong>IT Center for Science in Finland</strong>, as part of a hybrid HPC, AI, and quantum computing platform.</p>
<h3><strong>Quantum research</strong></h3>
<ul>
<li>A <strong>University of Chicago</strong> researcher found that a quantum computer could &#8220;use high-powered lasers as &#8216;optical tweezers&#8217; to capture and <a href="https://pme.uchicago.edu/news-events/news/helium-lifts-new-quantum-computing-concept">control individual atoms of helium</a>,&#8221; offering faster tunneling, faster transport, and controllable motional qubits, compared to designs based on lithium.</li>
<li>An <strong>MIT</strong> researcher tested <a href="https://openai.com/index/codex-quantum-computing-experiments/">GPT-5.6 Sol’s ability to run measurements</a> on an uncalibrated six-qubit chip and found that, when the signals were clear, Codex completed a standard sequence of measurements with little researcher intervention.</li>
</ul>
<hr />
<h2 id="Workforce, Education"><strong>Workforce, Education</strong></h2>
<p>The <strong>National Network for Microelectronics Education</strong> formed its first <a href="https://www.semi.org/en/semi-press-release/national-network-for-microelectronics-education-announces-inaugural-industry-advisory-committee-to-help-shape-americas-semiconductor-workforce-strategy">Industry Advisory Committee</a>, bringing together leaders from <strong>Lam Research, Intel </strong>and others to guide U.S. semiconductor workforce strategy. The group will help align education and training programs with industry needs as the sector faces a projected shortfall of 127,000 to 157,000 workers by 2030.</p>
<p><strong>India </strong>is <a href="https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/bhubaneswar/govt-enables-free-chip-design-tools-for-13-engg-colleges/articleshow/133927394.cms">providing EDA tools</a> to 13 engineering colleges under its chips to startup (C2S) program.</p>
<p>The <strong>U.S. State Department</strong> formally launched <a href="https://www.state.gov/releases/office-of-the-spokesperson/2026/09/trump-administration-launches-foundry-school-to-build-the-workforce-behind-americas-manufacturing-comeback">Foundry School,</a> a training program for engineers, technicians and industry leaders, with instruction spanning semiconductors, factory design, automation, supply chains and manufacturing operations.</p>

		<title>Redefining Processes At Sub-2nm</title>
		<link>https://semiengineering.com/redefining-processes-at-sub-2nm/</link>
					<comments>https://semiengineering.com/redefining-processes-at-sub-2nm/#respond</comments>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Ed Sperling]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Thu, 10 Sep 2026 07:13:52 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Test, Measurement and Analytics]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Top Stories]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[2nm]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[ATPG]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Bruker]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Lam Research]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Onto Innovation]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[PDF Solutions]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[process monitoring]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[proteanTecs]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[semiconductor manufacturing]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Siemens EDA]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Synopsys]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[test]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://semiengineering.com/?p=24281191</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p>Discrete steps are being merged with others as dimensions shrink into the angstrom range.</p>
<p>The post <a href="https://semiengineering.com/redefining-processes-at-sub-2nm/">Redefining Processes At Sub-2nm</a> appeared first on <a href="https://semiengineering.com">Semiconductor Engineering</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<p><strong>Key Takeaways:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Sub-2nm manufacturing is blurring traditional process boundaries as shrinking dimensions and tighter margins make test, metrology, inspection, and manufacturing increasingly interdependent.</li>
<li>More sensitivity creates more noise. Advanced inspection can detect millions of potential defects, making it harder to distinguish harmless process variation from issues that affect yield, reliability, or performance.</li>
<li>Data needs to flow back and forth across a chip&#8217;s entire lifecycle so it can be acted upon as needed.</li>
</ul>
<hr />
<p>The lines between discrete semiconductor manufacturing processes are starting to blur at sub-2nm nodes as transistors continue to shrink, sensitivity to various processes rises, and the amount of margin available to minimize problems disappears.</p>
<p>At these dimensions, a single atom can change how a chip behaves, and even a gentle wafer probe can damage an oxide layer or a via on a thinned substrate. Process variation can cause false error reporting in metrology. And a nano-sized particle that remains on a chip after removing a sacrificial material can turn an expensive multi-die stack into scrap.</p>
<p>&#8220;People are going from trying to probe chiplets to having sacrificial pads because they don&#8217;t want to damage the bumps that we&#8217;re actually going to bond to,&#8221; said Lee Harrison, director of automotive IC solutions at <a href="https://semiengineering.com/entities/mentor-a-siemens-business/">Siemens EDA</a>. &#8220;And now we&#8217;re seeing hybrid bonding, which is a super cool technology, but there&#8217;s no way you&#8217;re going to be able to probe a hybrid bond and keep it in one piece. We&#8217;re seeing some customers doing wafer bonding before test because you&#8217;re getting these extra-thin dies and extra-thin wafers.&#8221;</p>
<p>At older nodes, there was enough margin built into manufacturing processes to ignore these kinds of issues. Substrates were thicker, less prone to warpage, and structures were more stable. But below 2nm, many dies are collections of chiplets because demand for processing far exceeds the number of transistors that can be packed into a reticle-sized die. That increases thermal density, elevates structural stress, and generates a huge number of unknowns because different workloads can stress chips in different ways. At the same time, increasing the overall performance of a device requires everything to be smaller, thinner, and subsequently more fragile, creating a confusing array of overlapping and often contradictory needs.</p>
<p>Large AI data centers are fully aware of these issues, which is why they are migrating toward redundant server clusters. &#8220;You&#8217;re probably going to have some manufacturing problems, so we&#8217;re building solutions for redundancy,&#8221; said Rob Kruger, product management director for multi-die strategy and 3D IP at <a href="https://semiengineering.com/entities/synopsys-inc/">Synopsys</a>. &#8220;So you can have redundant clusters instead of redundant lanes and a 3D interconnect, because if you have a fault — it might take out a whole slew of faults, not just one — and then you have multi-die tests, you have to test these dies before you integrate and then after integration. There are some standards there, which are helping, and having hierarchical test servers on each die is becoming common. You can test before you package, after package, and then have capabilities to repair packages if there are problems using redundancy. They can do that for UCIe and for 3D connections.&#8221;</p>
<p>That effectively moves margin outside the individual dies within a package, enabling hot swapping of compute resources. Ironically, this approach originally was developed for mainframes and minicomputers several decades ago to reduce downtime, but it was largely abandoned in the 1990s with the introduction of inexpensive servers running Windows NT and various flavors of Unix.</p>
<p><strong>False positives</strong><br />
Shrinking features enabled the proliferation of cheap hardware, but the laws of physics are starting to reverse those cost benefits. Deploying exactly the same processes across a wafer can produce different results in different sectors of that wafer. And while this variation in processes is generally predictable, it can impact other processes that in the past were not affected.</p>
<p>&#8220;We are seeing an explosion in the number of defects detected on the wafer to millions of defects,&#8221; said Prasad Bachiraju, senior director of business development at <a href="https://semiengineering.com/entities/onto-innovation/">Onto Innovation</a>. &#8220;Because of the tool sensitivity, when you&#8217;re trying to capture the critical defect, it is actually capturing the neighborhood and the process variation also as a defect. That&#8217;s all noise and nuisance.&#8221;</p>
<p>Others agree. &#8220;What we are seeing is that advanced nodes are making the industry less able to rely on inspection signals alone to decide what matters electrically,&#8221; said Noam Brousard, vice president of solutions engineering at <a href="https://semiengineering.com/entities/proteantecs/">proteanTecs</a>. &#8220;At 2nm and below, the volume of potential indications can be enormous, and many signals may reflect local process variation rather than a defect that will become a functional or reliability problem.&#8221;</p>
<p>No single solution exists. Instead, multiple approaches are required to work in sync, under continuous monitoring, and each needs to be evaluated and implemented in the context of potential interactions with other solutions.</p>
<p>&#8220;One of the paradigm changes in how we monitor quality and health is that we are not tracking a single indicator, but a collection of many data points,&#8221; Brousard said. &#8220;Individual indicators, such as process variation, temperature, or voltage, may suggest an out-of-bounds condition, but they can also reflect normal variation rather than a true defect. As designs become more complex, there are more clues that may point to a defective part, but it is increasingly difficult to distinguish between harmless variation and a condition that will affect operation. You need to look at the end result — how the actual logic is being affected by the combination of many possible factors.&#8221;</p>
<p>In addition, there are more insertion points that can cause defects, and there is more data being produced than can be classified and processed using traditional cloud-based methods. The best way to comprehend that data is by abstracting it.</p>
<p>&#8220;The industry has shifted to virtual capabilities, and away from iterative work, to do R&amp;D,&#8221; said David Fried, chief AI officer and corporate vice president for Semiverse Solutions at <a href="https://semiengineering.com/entities/lam-research/">Lam Research</a>. &#8220;A lot of virtualization, modeling, and optimization has happened, so I have high hopes that the types of structures and technologies that are marching toward manufacturing in these nodes are designed in a more robust way than technologies of the past. Hopefully what that translates to is that we don&#8217;t have late showstopper-type problems in these technologies. It&#8217;s a challenge to ramp these technologies. The individual process variabilities are still going to be really challenging. Hundreds of processes have to come together, and you need to account for variations in all those processes. Historically, this has been done by just running scads of hardware through the fab and trying to use data measurement, metrology, and inspection to map out the boundaries of all these variations. But there is an amazing amount of process complexity. There are so many steps in the process that you just can&#8217;t map out the full space with hardware anymore.&#8221;</p>
<p><strong>Looking deeper, wider, and more often</strong><br />
There are no real surprises here. What&#8217;s changed is the sheer volume of things that need to be considered.</p>
<p>&#8220;Warpage is pretty well understood,&#8221; said Juliette Vandermeer, product marketing manager at <a href="https://semiengineering.com/entities/bruker/">Bruker Semiconductor</a>. &#8220;You know the process, you know what kind of silicon film you grow on the wafers, and you know, &#8216;Okay, this will warp that way.&#8217; But if something gets really warped, it also has microfractures.&#8221;</p>
<p>Finding those fractures requires looking much deeper into the various metal layers, often using X-ray diffraction imaging — also called X-ray tomography — to see and measure what&#8217;s actually happening inside a chip or package at each process stage or insertion point.</p>
<p>&#8220;The layers are getting thinner, so a higher precision is required,&#8221; Vandermeer said. &#8220;The challenge is really the thickness and the concentration, which is the growth process. There is temperature control during the growth, and interfacial roughness has an impact on the quality of the resistor channels. These are parameters we measure, and if there is an error at the front end, that can propagate to the very end. Our customers need to be certain that a process is well controlled. The process specs need to be tight, in the angstrom range, and our metrology specs need to be in the sub-angstrom range.&#8221;</p>
<p><img data-recalc-dims="1" fetchpriority="high" decoding="async" class="alignnone size-full wp-image-24281198" src="https://i0.wp.com/semiengineering.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Screenshot-2026-09-09-at-3.23.50-PM.png?resize=1120%2C770&#038;ssl=1" alt="" width="1120" height="770" srcset="https://i0.wp.com/semiengineering.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Screenshot-2026-09-09-at-3.23.50-PM.png?w=1120&amp;ssl=1 1120w, https://i0.wp.com/semiengineering.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Screenshot-2026-09-09-at-3.23.50-PM.png?resize=300%2C206&amp;ssl=1 300w, https://i0.wp.com/semiengineering.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Screenshot-2026-09-09-at-3.23.50-PM.png?resize=1024%2C704&amp;ssl=1 1024w, https://i0.wp.com/semiengineering.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Screenshot-2026-09-09-at-3.23.50-PM.png?resize=768%2C528&amp;ssl=1 768w, https://i0.wp.com/semiengineering.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Screenshot-2026-09-09-at-3.23.50-PM.png?resize=600%2C413&amp;ssl=1 600w" sizes="(max-width: 1000px) 100vw, 1000px" /><br />
<strong>Fig. 1: X-ray diffraction imaging can find defects in wafers that can cause catastrophic structural failure before breakage occurs. Source: Bruker</strong></p>
<p>This is more than just the overlapping of process steps during manufacturing. It&#8217;s a compression of the whole design-through-manufacturing chain, and beyond that into the field. Data needs to flow in multiple directions and be analyzed outside of traditional silos, and extracting that data requires more types of testing, inspection, and metrology equipment, as well as infrastructure to sort through all of it and take action in real-time.</p>
<p>&#8220;We&#8217;re starting to see a mixture,&#8221; said Siemens&#8217; Harrison. &#8220;The regular ATPG scan is still very dominant in the whole test strategy. You might have a couple thousand processing elements, so you would test your processing elements with ATPG. But if you&#8217;re doing some kind of core harvesting, then you might pick up another strategy, whether that&#8217;s BiST (built-in self-test) or some other kind of functional test, to do the reallocation of lanes or interconnect and things like that. And then, testing in the field is becoming a significant demand right now. I scoped out our original in-system deterministic test product back in 2019, where we had a couple of automotive customers asking us for better test quality than logic BiST. However, what&#8217;s happened is the guys doing the data centers have really taken hold of that technology, and they&#8217;re driving it forward using the kind of periodic testing they do on data centers to make sure everything is still working. They&#8217;re doing it to save a huge amount of cash in terms of being able to understand when to do that preventive maintenance instead of just guessing at it.&#8221;</p>
<p>Just setting limits on temperature or tracking the speed of data movement is no longer sufficient. What&#8217;s required is a hierarchical way to coordinate, interpret, and prioritize data at every phase of manufacturing and operation, and then determine where it will best be used.</p>
<p>&#8220;Margin Agents allow us to answer a more important question than temperature alone can answer,&#8221; said proteanTecs&#8217; Brousard. &#8220;They tell us how safe a specific buried domain actually is, not just how hot it is. That distinction matters significantly in a stacked structure. In a shingled or vertical stack, thermal coupling between layers can degrade the effective timing margin of a domain even when nothing inside that domain has changed. A neighboring tier may run hot; self-heating may increase the local temperature, and timing paths in the domain above or below it may lose margin as a result. A thermal sensor can tell you that temperature increased, but it cannot tell you whether that increase created an actual timing risk. The relationship between local heat and margin loss depends on which paths are affected, how they are routed relative to the hot layer, and what voltage they are running at.&#8221;</p>
<p>That might affect only a single die on a wafer, or it could affect an entire panel or advanced package.</p>
<p>&#8220;When a wafer is tested at the foundry, they don&#8217;t know where those chips are going to go to be packaged, assembled, and tested,&#8221; said John Kibarian, CEO of <a href="https://semiengineering.com/entities/pdf-solutions/">PDF Solutions</a>. &#8220;They&#8217;ve got to know where to go to send the material to take the human out of the loop. That&#8217;s really not something that&#8217;s gone on. We call that the orchestration layer. This is like a low-code or no-code way of connecting your apps. If you think about PLM, ERP, and MES systems, your engineering data, manufacturing yield data, and ultimately your design automation information, you need to be able to get that information in order to take the human out of the loop so AI can make appropriate decisions.&#8221;</p>
<p><strong>Conclusion</strong><br />
The smaller the features on a die, or the denser the package, the bigger the challenge in keeping track of everything. At each new node below 2nm, more testing, more precision, and more information about what&#8217;s going on at the surface and within a chip or package are all essential. But in addition to that, each process needs to include cross-over data and a level of awareness about what impact each step can have on other process steps, and what used to be defined spaces for testing, measuring, and inspecting are now a collection of overlapping combinations of steps that must be considered both individually and collectively.</p>
<hr />
<p><strong>Related Article</strong><br />
<a href="https://semiengineering.com/multi-die-assemblies-dominate-at-2nm-and-below/">Multi-Die Assemblies Dominate At 2nm And Below</a><br />
Chips are getting bigger, more modular, and much more capable as new innovations mix with existing processes and long-researched projects go mainstream.</p>
